dataset: Decision record - not a data file
notes: OEWS Research Estimates (OEWSRES24, NAICS 999200) SELECTED for Indicator 1; ASPEP24 NOT SELECTED. Reason: the spec permits the upgrade only if the research estimates cover the state-government sector at state level for all 51 with acceptable reliability. They do - 51 of 51 present, no suppressed cells, all MEAN_PRSE <= 0.2, all A_MEAN inside the plausibility band. ASPEP fails coverage: it has no state-government record for D.C. at all, because Census classifies D.C. as a municipal government. Using ASPEP would make I1 COULDNT_CHECK for D.C., cutting D.C.'s covered_weight to 0.68 and forcing an INSUFFICIENT verdict with no published D1 score, on the highest-weighted indicator. The two sources are NOT mixed: all 51 I1 values will come from OEWSRES24. OPEN CONSEQUENCE REQUIRING USER SIGN-OFF: this changes the I1 formula. The spec computes annual pay as (sum full-time March payroll / sum full-time employees) * 12 over a fixed seven-function basket. OEWSRES24 publishes A_MEAN directly in USD_annual for all state government excluding schools and hospitals, so there is no payroll-over-headcount step and no seven-function basket. The exclusion of schools and hospitals matches the spec's stated intent, but the basket is not reproducible in this source. Not implemented pending user approval.

dataset: Phase 2 decision record - not a data file
notes: APPROVED. The I4 plan-type rubric gains CB = 30, equal to HYBRID. Rationale: cash-balance plans pool investment risk with an employer-guaranteed credit, which sits structurally between DB and DC, so HYBRID's 30 is the closest fit. Full plan-type rubric is therefore DB 40, HYBRID 30, CB 30, CHOICE 25, DC 15. Added to rule R5 BEFORE any CB jurisdiction was extracted and applied blind to all 51; the value was not revisited after seeing its effect. Four jurisdictions carry CB for general employees: Kansas, Kentucky, Nebraska and Texas. Texas was not among the three anticipated - its 2024 tier is cash balance for state employees hired after 8/31/22 - and it was scored under the same rule without adjustment.

dataset: Phase 3 decision record - not a data file
notes: FIRST REFINEMENT of rule R6 (Social Security coverage). Original R6 mapped any 'X, except Y' wording to PARTIAL, understating coverage where the exception fell on a class R3 already excludes. Restated: an exception affecting ONLY classes excluded by R3 does not reduce coverage; where it reaches any part of the general-employee population, PARTIAL applies at 20. Derivable from R3's own scoping and chosen without knowledge of which jurisdictions it affects. Implemented as a blind mechanical classifier (work/r6_refined.py) with no jurisdiction names in it. OUTCOME: five of six expected states moved (Kansas, Minnesota, New Hampshire, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island); Oregon correctly did NOT move (its exception is employer-elected and names no class); Kentucky moved the WRONG WAY, PARTIAL to NOT_COVERED, because its exception names university members. That unpredicted move triggered the stop-condition and led to Decision 8.

dataset: Phase 3 decision record - not a data file
notes: SECOND REFINEMENT of rule R6. Root cause: R3's exclusion list serves TWO distinct purposes and R6 was reading both. POPULATION-SCOPE entries name classes genuinely outside the general-employee population; RATE-PURITY entries name classes that ARE general employees but whose distinct rate figures must be kept out of the general rate. R6 inherits population-scope exclusions ONLY. University members are rate-purity and were dropped from R6's list. R6 list now: public safety, police, fire, state patrol/troopers, judiciary, teachers. AUDIT OF DROPPED/AMBIGUOUS ENTRIES: corrections, sheriffs, law enforcement, custodial and legislators are arguably population-scope but were not adjudicated, so they are NOT kept; this ambiguity is FLAGGED rather than silently decided. None of those tokens appears in any of the 51 raw Social Security strings, so the ambiguity is moot for this build and is recorded for a future rebuild. Re-run blind across all 51: exactly ONE jurisdiction moved, Kentucky NOT_COVERED -> PARTIAL, as predicted; no unpredicted moves; the five from the first refinement were undisturbed at COVERED and Oregon remained PARTIAL.
